q: A Kingdom is a subdivision of a _____.
e: A Kingdom is a subdivision of a Domain. Domains sit above kingdoms: Bacteria, Archaea, and Eukarya. Class would fill a different blank than Domain.

q: All living organisms are classified into _____ domains.
e: All living organisms are classified into three domains. Three is the idea that completes this fact. Six would fill a different blank than three.

q: Living organisms are currently divided into _____ kingdoms.
e: Living organisms are currently divided into six kingdoms. A common six-kingdom set is Eubacteria, Archaebacteria, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia. Three would fill a different blank than six.

q: The domains Archaea and Bacteria contain the kingdoms Archaebacteria and _____.
e: The domains Archaea and Bacteria contain the kingdoms Archaebacteria and Eubacteria. Eubacteria are prokaryotes with a relatively simple cell structure. Fungi would fill a different blank than Eubacteria.

q: Within the domain Eukarya, there are _____ kingdoms.
e: Within the domain Eukarya, there are four kingdoms. Four is the idea that completes this fact. Three would fill a different blank than four.

q: Archaebacteria are primitive, unicellular prokaryotes that live in _____ environments.
e: Archaebacteria are primitive, unicellular prokaryotes that live in extreme environments. Archaea often live in harsh places such as hot springs or very salty water. Moist terrestrial would fill a different blank than extreme.

q: Organisms belonging to kingdom Archaebacteria are obligate _____.
e: Organisms belonging to kingdom Archaebacteria are obligate anaerobes. Anaerobes is the idea that completes this fact. Parasites would fill a different blank than anaerobes.

q: Cyanobacteria belong to the kingdom _____.
e: Cyanobacteria belong to the kingdom Eubacteria. Eubacteria are prokaryotes with a relatively simple cell structure. Protista would fill a different blank than Eubacteria.

q: Eubacteria reproduce asexually by _____.
e: Eubacteria reproduce asexually by fission. Fission is the idea that completes this fact. Fragmentation would fill a different blank than fission.

q: Size of non-cellular virus particles ranges from _____.
e: Size of non-cellular virus particles ranges from 20-400 ext nm. 20-400 ext nm is the idea that completes this fact. 20-400 ext mm would fill a different blank than 20-400 ext nm.

q: Viruses consist of DNA or RNA genetic material covered by a _____ coat.
e: Viruses consist of DNA or RNA genetic material covered by a protein coat. Protein is the idea that completes this fact. Lipid would fill a different blank than protein.

q: Outside of living host cells, viruses _____ survive.
e: Outside of living host cells, viruses cannot survive. Cannot is the idea that completes this fact. Can easily would fill a different blank than cannot.

q: The term 'protist' refers to any _____ organism that is not a plant, animal, or fungus.
e: The term 'protist' refers to any eukaryotic organism that is not a plant, animal, or fungus. Eukaryotic cells keep their DNA inside a nucleus. Prokaryotic is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: Approximately _____ species of protists have been described.
e: Approximately 60,000 species of protists have been described. 60,000 is the idea that completes this fact. 600,000 would fill a different blank than 60,000.

q: In protists, excess water is removed from the cell by the _____.
e: In protists, excess water is removed from the cell by the contractile vacuole. Contractile vacuole is the idea that completes this fact. Nucleus would fill a different blank than contractile vacuole.

q: Plant-like protists contain chlorophyll in chloroplasts and are classified as _____.
e: Plant-like protists contain chlorophyll in chloroplasts and are classified as autotrophs. Autotrophs is the idea that completes this fact. Saprophytes would fill a different blank than autotrophs.

q: Fungus-like protists lack _____ in their cell walls.
e: Fungus-like protists lack chitin in their cell walls. Fungal cell walls are made of chitin. Cellulose would fill a different blank than chitin.

q: The phylum Chlorophyta includes unicellular photosynthetic protists such as _____.
e: The phylum Chlorophyta includes unicellular photosynthetic protists such as Chlorella. Chlorella is the idea that completes this fact. Euglena would fill a different blank than Chlorella.

q: Protists in the division Chrysophyta manufacture the carbohydrate _____.
e: Protists in the division Chrysophyta manufacture the carbohydrate chrysolaminarin. Chrysolaminarin is the idea that completes this fact. Starch would fill a different blank than chrysolaminarin.

q: The shell of Chrysophyta (e.g., diatoms) is uniquely composed of _____.
e: The shell of Chrysophyta (e.g., diatoms) is uniquely composed of silica. Silica is the idea that completes this fact. Calcium carbonate would fill a different blank than silica.

q: Protists that move by pseudopodia, lack chromatophores, and possess a single nucleus belong to _____.
e: Protists that move by pseudopodia, lack chromatophores, and possess a single nucleus belong to Rhizopoda. Rhizopoda is the idea that completes this fact. Actinopoda would fill a different blank than Rhizopoda.

q: Protists having glassy skeletons and needle-like pseudopods belong to the phylum _____.
e: Protists having glassy skeletons and needle-like pseudopods belong to the phylum Actinopoda. Actinopoda is the idea that completes this fact. Rhizopoda would fill a different blank than Actinopoda.

q: Foraminiferans move by means of _____.
e: Foraminiferans move by means of protoplasmic streaming. Protoplasmic streaming is the idea that completes this fact. Cilia would fill a different blank than protoplasmic streaming.

q: A collection of thread-like filaments forming the body of fungi is known as _____.
e: A collection of thread-like filaments forming the body of fungi is known as mycelia. Mycelia is the idea that completes this fact. Hyphae would fill a different blank than mycelia.

q: The cell wall of fungal hyphae is made up of _____.
e: The cell wall of fungal hyphae is made up of chitin. Fungal cell walls are made of chitin. Peptidoglycan would fill a different blank than chitin.

q: Fungi that have coenocytic (aseptate) hyphae and belong to the simplest, most primitive group are _____.
e: Fungi that have coenocytic (aseptate) hyphae and belong to the simplest, most primitive group are Chytridiomycota. Chytridiomycota is the idea that completes this fact. Zygomycota would fill a different blank than Chytridiomycota.

q: Zygomycota form a _____ during sexual reproduction.
e: Zygomycota form a zygospore during sexual reproduction. Zygospore is the idea that completes this fact. Basidium would fill a different blank than zygospore.

q: Sac fungi belong to the division _____.
e: Sac fungi belong to the division Ascomycota. Ascomycota is the idea that completes this fact. Basidiomycota would fill a different blank than Ascomycota.

q: Yeast is an example of unicellular fungus belonging to _____.
e: Yeast is an example of unicellular fungus belonging to Ascomycota. Ascomycota is the idea that completes this fact. Basidiomycota would fill a different blank than Ascomycota.

q: Club fungi possess club-shaped fruiting bodies called _____.
e: Club fungi possess club-shaped fruiting bodies called basidia. Basidia is the idea that completes this fact. Conidia would fill a different blank than basidia.

q: Deuteromycota are known as imperfect fungi because they undergo strictly _____ reproduction.
e: Deuteromycota are known as imperfect fungi because they undergo strictly asexual reproduction. Asexual reproduction makes offspring from one parent without gametes fusing. Conjugated would fill a different blank than asexual.

q: An example of Deuteromycota (imperfect fungi) given in the textbook is _____.
e: An example of Deuteromycota (imperfect fungi) given in the textbook is Penicillium. Penicillium is the idea that completes this fact. Yeast would fill a different blank than Penicillium.

q: The cell wall of plants is composed of _____.
e: The cell wall of plants is composed of cellulose. Plant cell walls are made of cellulose. Silica would fill a different blank than cellulose.

q: The division Thallophyta includes simple plant bodies called thallus which lack a _____ system.
e: The division Thallophyta includes simple plant bodies called thallus which lack a vascular system. Vascular is the idea that completes this fact. Reproductive would fill a different blank than vascular.

q: The most primitive land plants belonging to Bryophyta anchor themselves with thread-like _____.
e: The most primitive land plants belonging to Bryophyta anchor themselves with thread-like rhizoids. Rhizoids is the idea that completes this fact. Roots would fill a different blank than rhizoids.

q: The regular alternation between gametophytic and sporophytic generations in Bryophyta is called _____.
e: The regular alternation between gametophytic and sporophytic generations in Bryophyta is called alternation of generations. Alternation of generations is the idea that completes this fact. Binary fission would fill a different blank than alternation of generations.

q: Pteridophytes are differentiated into _____.
e: Pteridophytes are differentiated into rhizome, rachis and pinna. Rhizome, rachis and pinna is the idea that completes this fact. Thallus and rhizoid would fill a different blank than rhizome, rachis and pinna.

q: Woody, non-flowering seed plants whose seeds are not enclosed in a fruit belong to _____.
e: Woody, non-flowering seed plants whose seeds are not enclosed in a fruit belong to Gymnospermae. Gymnospermae is the idea that completes this fact. Angiospermae is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: Flowering vascular plants whose seeds are produced inside the ovary of the flower are _____.
e: Flowering vascular plants whose seeds are produced inside the ovary of the flower are Angiospermae. Angiospermae is the idea that completes this fact. Thallophyta would fill a different blank than Angiospermae.

q: Monocotyledonous seeds contain _____ cotyledon.
e: Monocotyledonous seeds contain one cotyledon. One is the idea that completes this fact. Two would fill a different blank than one.

q: Invertebrates make up more than _____ percent of all animal species alive today.
e: Invertebrates make up more than 95 percent of all animal species alive today. 95 is the idea that completes this fact. 50 would fill a different blank than 95.

q: Animals belonging to phylum Porifera are non-motile (sessile) pore-filter feeders with _____ symmetry.
e: Animals belonging to phylum Porifera are non-motile (sessile) pore-filter feeders with asymmetrical symmetry. Asymmetrical is the idea that completes this fact. Radial would fill a different blank than asymmetrical.

q: The body plan of Cnidarians includes a sessile polyp or a motile _____.
e: The body plan of Cnidarians includes a sessile polyp or a motile medusa. Medusa is the idea that completes this fact. Pinna would fill a different blank than medusa.

q: All organisms belonging to phylum Cnidaria possess specialized _____ cells.
e: All organisms belonging to phylum Cnidaria possess specialized stinging cells. Stinging is the idea that completes this fact. Flagellated would fill a different blank than stinging.

q: Platyhelminthes are flatworms that lack a body cavity, making them _____.
e: Platyhelminthes are flatworms that lack a body cavity, making them acoelomate. Acoelomate is the idea that completes this fact. Pseudocoelomate would fill a different blank than acoelomate.

q: Roundworms belong to phylum Nematoda and possess a body cavity called a _____.
e: Roundworms belong to phylum Nematoda and possess a body cavity called a pseudocoelomate. Pseudocoelomate is the idea that completes this fact. Gastrovascular cavity would fill a different blank than pseudocoelomate.

q: Annelids (e.g. earthworms) are characterized by having a segmented body and a _____.
e: Annelids (e.g. earthworms) are characterized by having a segmented body and a true coelom. True coelom is the idea that completes this fact. Pseudocoelom would fill a different blank than true coelom.

q: Soft-bodied animals that may or may not possess a shell (such as snails and squids) belong to phylum _____.
e: Soft-bodied animals that may or may not possess a shell (such as snails and squids) belong to phylum Mollusca. Mollusca is the idea that completes this fact. Arthropoda is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: Animals with jointed appendages and an exoskeleton belong to phylum _____.
e: Animals with jointed appendages and an exoskeleton belong to phylum Arthropoda. Arthropoda is the idea that completes this fact. Echinodermata would fill a different blank than Arthropoda.

q: Centipedes possess _____ pair(s) of legs per segment.
e: Centipedes possess one pair(s) of legs per segment. One is the idea that completes this fact. Three would fill a different blank than one.

q: Echinoderms exhibit bilateral symmetry in their embryo stage and _____ symmetry in adults.
e: Echinoderms exhibit bilateral symmetry in their embryo stage and radial symmetry in adults. Radial is the idea that completes this fact. Bilateral would fill a different blank than radial.

q: A unique feature of phylum Echinodermata used for movement is the _____ system.
e: An unique feature of phylum Echinodermata used for movement is the water vascular system. Water vascular is the idea that completes this fact. Circulatory would fill a different blank than water vascular.

q: All chordates possess a dorsal hollow nerve cord, pharyngeal gill slits, a tail, and a _____.
e: All chordates possess a dorsal hollow nerve cord, pharyngeal gill slits, a tail, and a notochord. Notochord is the idea that completes this fact. Vertebra would fill a different blank than notochord.

q: Cold-blooded animals whose body temperature changes with the environment are termed _____.
e: Cold-blooded animals whose body temperature changes with the environment are termed poikilothermic. Poikilothermic is the idea that completes this fact. Endothermic would fill a different blank than poikilothermic.

q: Amphibian larvae breathe through _____ while adult amphibians breathe through lungs.
e: Amphibian larvae breathe through gills while adult amphibians breathe through lungs. Gills is the idea that completes this fact. Trachea would fill a different blank than gills.

q: Warm-blooded animals that maintain a constant body temperature are termed _____.
e: Warm-blooded animals that maintain a constant body temperature are termed homoiothermic. Homoiothermic is the idea that completes this fact. Ectothermic would fill a different blank than homoiothermic.

q: Birds are homoiothermic vertebrates whose forelimbs are modified into _____ for flight.
e: Birds are homoiothermic vertebrates whose forelimbs are modified into wings for flight. Wings is the idea that completes this fact. Legs would fill a different blank than wings.

q: Mammals are distinguished by having body hair, a placenta, and _____ glands to feed young.
e: Mammals are distinguished by having body hair, a placenta, and mammary glands to feed young. Mammary is the idea that completes this fact. Salivary would fill a different blank than mammary.

q: In mammals, respiration is aided by lungs and a muscle sheet called the _____.
e: In mammals, respiration is aided by lungs and a muscle sheet called the diaphragm. Diaphragm is the idea that completes this fact. Placenta would fill a different blank than diaphragm.
